root_idea.summary: The root centers on water emerging and on the source or outlet from which it flows, alongside a distinct lexical branch naming the nabʿ tree.
root_idea.development: The water branch extends from welling or issuing forth to the spring or source itself, with a causative Form IV verb meaning to make water issue. The lexica separately preserve نَبْع as a tree name and related terms for objects made from its wood.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular noun citation form يَنْبُوع; the Quran also contains its plural يَنَابِيع.

senses.definition: A spring or water-source from which water emerges.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a natural water source; the Quranic occurrences include the singular يَنْبُوعًا and the plural يَنَابِيعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To well or issue forth, specifically of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive verbal use describing water emerging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or cause water to issue forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV verbal construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nabʿ tree, whose wood was used for making bows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun distinct from the water-source noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two shafts of a cart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: So called because such shafts were commonly made from nabʿ wood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The places on a camel from which its sweat flows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-specific lexical expression for the outlets of perspiration.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The water-welling verb is represented under the Classical verbal meaning.
